Knowledge Graph Structure

Frontier-Exploration---AI-Generated-Cont.title: Frontier Exploration - AI-Generated Content Verification
Frontier-Exploration---AI-Generated-Cont.content:
Frontier Exploration - AI-Generated Content Verification
The Gap
The Seed covers:

Source citation requirements
Confidence markers
Procedural knowledge verification
AI-optimized knowledge structures

But there’s no explicit guidance on: How to verify that content generated by AI assistants is accurate before adding it to the vault.
Why This Matters
As AI assistants become partners in knowledge base building:

AI can generate plausible-sounding but incorrect information (hallucinations)
AI may cite sources that don’t exist or misquote real sources
AI-generated content needs the same verification as human-generated content
Without verification rules, the vault could accumulate inaccurate knowledge

The Problem for AI Agents
When an AI generates a note:

AI writes: “Vitamin D helps with depression” with a citation
How does the human verify this is accurate?
The Seed says “cite sources” but doesn’t say “verify AI-cited sources”
The AI might hallucinate the citation entirely

Current Guidance Gaps
Gap 1: No Verification Workflow
The Seed has verification-status: unverified | tested | community-validated but:

Who verifies AI-generated content?
What’s the minimum verification required?
Can AI self-verify, or does it need human oversight?

Gap 2: Source Hallucination Detection
AI might produce citations like:

“Study published in Journal of X (2023)” that doesn’t exist
Misquoted findings
Real studies with incorrect conclusions attributed

Gap 3: Confidence Appropriate for AI Generation
If AI generates content with 80% confidence, what should the note’s confidence marker be?
Proposed Rules
Rule 1: AI-Generated Content Tagging
Rule: Notes partially or fully generated by AI must include author-type: AI-assisted | AI-first-pass | human-only in frontmatter.
Why: Readers (and other AIs) need to know the provenance of the content to assess reliability.
Test: Can you identify which notes were AI-generated? Is each marked appropriately?
Rule 2: Minimum Verification for AI Content
Rule: AI-generated notes require at minimum ONE form of verification before marking as verified:

Cross-reference with trusted source
Human review acknowledgment
Comparison with established databases

Why: AI hallucinations can appear confident but be completely wrong. Verification is non-optional.
Test: For AI-generated notes, is there verification documentation? Can you trace how accuracy was confirmed?
Rule 3: Source Verification Requirement
Rule: For AI-generated notes, at least one cited source must be spot-checked (open the URL, verify the claim exists).
Why: AI can hallucinate citations entirely. Spot-checking prevents false attribution.
Test: Can you verify at least one source in AI-generated notes is real and accurately cited?
Rule 4: Confidence Adjustment
Rule: AI-generated content should start at confidence: emerging unless verified by a human, regardless of how the AI rates its own confidence.
Why: AI confidence is not calibrated to human reliability. A confident AI hallucination is more dangerous than an AI admitting uncertainty.
Test: Do AI-generated notes show appropriate confidence (not “high” without human verification)?
Verification Workflow
For AI-Assisted Notes (Human writes, AI helps):

Human creates draft with AI assistance
Mark as author-type: AI-assisted
Human verifies key claims
Set confidence based on verification level

For AI-First-Pass Notes (AI writes, human reviews):

AI generates initial note
Mark as author-type: AI-first-pass
Human performs spot-check verification
Update to author-type: human-verified after verification
Set confidence appropriately

For Critical Domain Content:

Medical, legal, financial AI-generated content requires expert review
Mark with review-required: expert for domain-critical content

Edge Cases
Edge Case 1: AI Improving Existing Notes
An AI suggests edits to a human-written note. Is this “AI-generated”?

Solution: Track diffs, verify significant changes, maintain human as primary author

Edge Case 2: AI Generating Based on Verified Sources
AI synthesizes from verified sources - is this still “AI-generated”?

Solution: Mark as AI-synthesized but note source verification status

Edge Case 3: Multiple AI Iterations
Note goes through AI → human → AI → human. What’s the author type?

Solution: Use author-type: collaborative with iteration history in notes

Edge Case 4: AI Confidence Calibration
AI says “99% confident” - should confidence reflect this?

Solution: No. AI confidence != reliable confidence. Default to emerging unless verified.

Interaction with Other Rules

Verification status: AI-generated notes should show verification process
Confidence markers: AI confidence should not override appropriate skepticism
Source validation: AI sources need extra verification, not less
Procedural content: AI-generated procedures need testing before “tested” status

Test for AI Agents
Given a note that may be AI-generated:

Is there author-type frontmatter?
Is there verification documentation?
Can you spot-check at least one source?
Is confidence appropriate for verification level?
For critical domains, is expert review documented?

Related

AI-Assisted Knowledge Management Seed — Core Seed rules and verification-status field
Handling Temporal Knowledge — Source verification methods
Confidence Markers — Confidence level guidance
Frontier Exploration - AI-Optimized Knowledge Bases — AI-native knowledge structures
Stress Test - Source Quality Hierarchy in Medical Knowledge — Source quality in practice

Questions for Seed Refinement

Should the Seed mandate human verification for all AI-generated content?
What’s the minimum verification standard for different confidence levels?
How should we handle AI-generated content in different domains (low-stakes vs high-stakes)?
Should there be a “verification chain” documenting how accuracy was confirmed?

Frontier-Exploration---AI-Optimized-Know.title: Frontier Exploration - AI-Optimized Knowledge Bases
Frontier-Exploration---AI-Optimized-Know.content:
Frontier Exploration - AI-Optimized Knowledge Bases

How should knowledge bases be structured when the primary consumer is an AI agent rather than a human?

The Problem Space
The current Seed assumes human readers who can:

Follow natural language explanations
Ask clarifying questions when confused
Infer context from headings and structure
Skip around non-linearly with understanding

AI agents have different needs:

Retrieval precision: AI needs exact matches, not “close enough”
Unambiguous semantics: Same term must mean same thing
Explicit prerequisites: AI cannot “just know” background context
Machine-readable structure: Frontmatter and tags must be parseable
Verification pathways: AI needs to validate claims, not just cite them

Key Distinctions
Human-Native vs AI-Native Knowledge



































AspectHuman-NativeAI-NativeExplanation styleNarrative, layered, exploratoryDeclarative, structured, completeContextInferred from experienceMust be explicitly providedAmbiguityTolerated, resolved by askingMust be eliminated upfrontLinksNavigation aidsSemantic contractsExamplesIllustrative, engagingVerifiable, testable
Retrieval vs Comprehension
Human knowledge bases optimize for comprehension - humans can piece together meaning from partial information.
AI knowledge bases optimize for retrieval - the AI needs to find exactly what it needs and trust it’s accurate.
This changes:

How atomicity is defined (AI needs complete units, not “one idea” - what is an “idea” to a machine?)
How links work (semantic contracts, not suggestions)
How confidence is communicated (probabilities AI can compute with, not vague markers)

Emerging Rules
Rule: Define semantic contracts for every link
For AI-native vaults, links should be explicit semantic contracts:

“This note defines term X used in the source note”
“This note provides evidence for claim Y”
“This note is a prerequisite for understanding Z”

Test: Can an AI determine why it should follow each link without reading both notes?
Rule: Separate assertion from evidence
Human notes mix claims and support. AI notes should structure:

Claims: standalone factual statements
Evidence: separate notes with verification data
Synthesis: notes that combine claims with source attribution

Test: Can an AI verify a claim by following evidence links without the source text?
Rule: Use formal ontology for key relationships
Beyond wikilinks, AI-native vaults need typed relationships:

is-a: taxonomy membership
part-of: composition
contradicts: opposing claims
supports: evidence relationship
prerequisites: dependency

Test: Can an AI answer “what does this note contradict?” by querying relationships?
Rule: Optimize for semantic search, not keyword matching
AI retrieval (RAG) uses embeddings, not exact text match. Structure affects retrieval:

Distinctive terminology (not generic “important” words)
Key concepts in first 100 words
Clear topic sentences
Minimal homonyms

Test: Does a semantic search for this note’s core concept return it as top result?
Domain-Specific Considerations
Prompt Engineering Knowledge
Prompts are procedural knowledge but with unique characteristics:

Exact wording matters (small changes = big output differences)
Context windows limit what can be included
Prompt versions should be tracked like code

Model Fine-Tuning Data
Knowledge for training differs from knowledge for retrieval:

Needs consistent formatting
Quality annotations matter more
Diversity must be explicit

Multi-Agent Knowledge
When multiple AI agents access the vault:

Version conflicts matter more
Locking/concurrency considerations
Audit trails for changes

Test Scenario

An AI agent must answer: “What’s the best way to cook salmon?”
From a human-native KB: Agent finds notes about salmon, cooking methods, reads several, synthesizes answer
From an AI-native KB: Agent finds verified procedural note with exact temps, times, confidence level, contradiction links to less-effective methods

Which produces more reliable results? The AI-native approach trades flexibility for precision.
Open Questions

Can one vault serve both human and AI readers well, or are these fundamentally incompatible?
How do we verify AI-native knowledge is actually retrievable by AI systems?
Should AI-native notes include the prompt that would retrieve them?

Related

AI-Assisted Knowledge Management Seed
Stress Test - Atomicity Rule Across Domains
AI-Assisted Knowledge Management Seed — verification-status rule for procedural content
AI-Assisted Knowledge Management Seed — verification-status field

This is frontier exploration territory. The rules here are hypotheses, not proven guidance. Test them. Refine them. If they fail, update or remove them.
